method: Original source-face tags through Boolean union/difference; real per-face color, no textures.

rules.name: Unknown closure and manufacturing
rules.note: Solid interiors, hidden flat roofs, generic model plinth and simplified grade; neutral does not imply a measured finish.

rules.name: Complete north–south high hall
rules.note: Includes the smaller northern court/block, separate northern roof pair and break in facade rhythm; no measured scale.

rules.name: Unequal stepped west entrance wing
rules.note: Lower annex steps farther west toward south; asymmetrical, not a symmetric podium. All precise depths approximate.

rules.name: Four paired east–west monitor groups
rules.note: Eight north–south triangular profiles in four groups; high glazed faces south. Pitches and subdivisions simplified; not north-light.

rules.name: Continuous raised west roof-edge plane
rules.note: High red-brown west plane conceals sawtooth ends in direct west elevation. Hidden joints and exact slope changes unknown.

rules.name: Recessed west glass entry and triangular lintel
rules.note: Two round columns, actual recessed porch, red triangular framing and light glazing grid. Thickened for model.

rules.name: Rounded stair/transition ends and south attachment interface
rules.note: South rounded capsule and north west-ended capsule retained. Closed shallow south attachment interface only, no free-ended bridge.

rules.name: South external stair and design-supported north counterpart
rules.note: South near east end; north simplified from design sheet. Solid supporting stair enclosures, not detailed engineered stairs.

rules.name: Facade-specific high hall window rhythms
rules.note: South broad upper band and largely blank lower wall; east repeated upper/lower groups and north distinct lower layout. North/east design-supported, not photographed as-built.

rules.name: West wing rooftop frames and sunken edge
rules.note: Small roof skylight/frame volumes, lower wall bands and visible basement/retaining edge simplified. No exact ground-level reconstruction.
